# Ranges the extension cannot honour

Every shape below is a range mark the extension has to refuse. It refuses each
one the same way: the mark still indexes its term, as an ordinary locator at
its own page, and the author is told what the index will show instead. The
refusal is not politeness — makeindex writes a transcript warning for an
unmatched, extra or inconsistently encapsulated range, and Quarto fails a
render on exactly that warning, so a range this extension cannot pair must
never reach the index tool at all.

Each shape uses a term no other shape uses, so a report reading one cannot be
satisfied by another's mark.

## An opening that is never closed

The discussion of [fenrir]{.index range="open"} begins here and the document
never says where it ends.

## A closing with no opening

A closing mark whose term was never opened: [golem]{.index range="close"}.

## A second opening while a range is still open

The discussion of [hydra]{.index range="open"} begins here, and a second
opening arrives for the same term before the first is closed:
[hydra]{.index range="open"}. The first opening is the one that pairs with the
closing below; the second is the mark that is reported.

The discussion of [hydra]{.index range="close"} ends here.

## A range mark that also carries a cross-reference

A cross-reference takes the place of a locator, and a range IS a locator — a
span of one — so a mark carrying both is asking for two things that occupy one
slot: [imp]{.index range="open" see="golem"}.

## A value that is neither an opening nor a closing

A `range=` value naming neither end: [jinn]{.index range="middle"}.

# The controls these reports must leave alone

A well-formed range, whose two marks must draw no report at all. The discussion
of [lamia]{.index range="open"} begins here and the discussion of
[lamia]{.index range="close"} ends here.

And an ordinary mark carrying no `range=` at all: [kelpie]{.index}.
